rows.what the ink shows: An opening curved stroke and a separate right parenthesis enclose an angular E: its rising upper arm and short middle arm remain visible above the cancellation loop.

A hooked left boundary and right curved parenthesis survive. The internal upper bar and diagonal descending stroke are crossed by a thick horizontal cancellation, so the central t is not securely distinguished from an angular E.
The first group begins with a high curved stroke returning into a small loop; the later group ends with an upright t-like stem. The intervening joins and the p are merged with the cancellation line.

The first surviving group contains a low enclosed s-like loop followed by an open e-shaped return, then a gap before the next joined bowls. These support tentative se, while the strike conceals the upper strokes; the following word remains unreadable.
The initial P has a tall descending stem and a distinct upper loop. The following a/r-sized joins run into the heavy strike and cannot be separated confidently.
The remaining word is almost wholly covered at baseline; one small rising hook, low oval remnants and a detached dot survive. These fragments do not determine the letter sequence.
The opening p has a long stem and a closed lower return, followed by a low join and a detached i dot. The later tall curve and terminal loop are crossed over, leaving the s/q/u/e sequence uncertain.

Multiple cancellation strokes cover the first group; farther right only a short diagonal mark, a low horizontal trace and a final hooked dip remain below the long strike. No complete word can be identified from these remnants.
An open initial c and a small loop with a detached dot/accent survive; the long cancellation merges most of the middle and final linked strokes, so the complete word is not secure.
The first character has two B lobes, followed by an E with a middle arm; the final tall crossed H is enclosed by curved parenthesis strokes despite the cancellation.
After FBE, the deleted glyph has a vertical/looped core and rightward upper strokes, but two heavy rising diagonals merge the letter contours and do not securely establish F.
The first raised letter has the lower return of E; the second has a descending stem with top and middle bars but no lower return, matching the clear F in the adjacent E,F superscript.

Five baseline letters are separately visible: E, B, F, B, E. The raised sign above F has a hooked angular top and a dark crossing/short lower stroke; unlike the clearer nearby 2 forms, this does not securely exclude a looped star.

The baseline sequence is E, B, E, with one small curved raised 2 after B. A broad cancellation loop crosses before the first E and below the last, preventing secure separation of either parenthesis from deletion strokes.
Three subscript baseline letters have B lobes, F stem/two bars, then B lobes; there is no raised star in the space between the first B and F.
Both raised letters have separate top bars, middle arms and curved lower returns; the second has the lower E stroke absent from the F in the preceding formula.

Five baseline positions read E, A, a looped upright, A, E. The pointed blot is raised above/right of the central upright and has no baseline stem, placing the star after that letter; its F arms remain merged with deletion, unlike the separable arms of nearby uncanceled F.

A rising lower sweep and pointed right junction survive, but the horizontal cancellation passes through the putative upper branch and lower bar. The full relation cannot be separated reliably from those strokes.
The lower closed angular loop is followed above and to the right by an E with a curved left side and short horizontal arms; cancellation crosses both without removing those outlines.
At the right end is a small triangular outline with a rising left side and a dark horizontal base; a long deletion arc passes behind its right side.
A rounded d and tall ascender lead into low connected r/n strokes, followed by a dotted i and a separate accent above the ending. No internal x crossing supports deuxième.
The opening has a descending p loop followed by a long low connected sequence and a pointed v near its right end. The opening lacks the tall crossed t required by toujours.

The upper stroke has a distinct short rising arm at its left and then turns into a lower rightward arm; a separate short bar sits below. That angled upper stroke distinguishes the sign from two parallel equality bars.
To the right of the equality sign stands one thick upright stroke with a small top hook and a heavy lower end. No loop or second stem is present.
